evidence.methodology_note: Rubric frozen below is intended to be applied identically to all 10 languages by whichever workers score them; this shard applies it only to TypeScript per its assignment.

rubric.description: 0-100 score = sum of four 0-25 sub-scores covering the core toolchain a working developer needs day-to-day: (1) official/primary compiler-or-runtime toolchain maturity and active maintenance, (2) formatter availability/adoption of a standard tool, (3) linter availability/adoption of a standard tool, (4) test runner + debugger + build-tool integration maturity. Same four sub-checks and same source types (official docs, release notes, and independent 2026 comparison articles) are to be used for every language.

citations: TypeScript 6.0 is the last release built on the original TypeScript/JavaScript codebase and acts as a bridge that deprecates a few features to align with the new compiler.
Microsoft has released TypeScript 7.0, featuring a native compiler that improves build speeds by 8x to 12x.
On the VS Code source, a full build fell from 125.7 seconds on TypeScript 6 to 10.6 seconds, an 11.9x improvement, while aggregate memory use dropped by around 18 percent.
compiler_toolchain.rationale: tsc is Microsoft's official, actively maintained compiler. It shipped a from-scratch native rewrite (Project Corsa) in 2026, delivering large measured speedups while preserving semantics.

citations: Biome is the most significant development in the JS/TS tooling space in years.
Start with Prettier (least controversial), then ESLint with minimal rules, then TypeScript in allowJs mode, and finally strict type checking.
formatter.rationale: Prettier is the long-standing de facto standard formatter with near-universal adoption; a Rust-based competitor (Biome) has emerged with strong 2026 traction, indicating a healthy but still-consolidating formatter landscape rather than a single unquestioned default.

citations: Even after I adopted a Rust-based linter, I had to keep using ESLint for lint rules such as the React Compiler plugin.
Oxlint is the first new linter that can run ESLint plugins directly via an ESLint plugin shim and NAPI-RS.
linter.rationale: ESLint plus typescript-eslint is the entrenched standard linter with an extensive plugin ecosystem that newer Rust-based linters (Oxlint) still shim into rather than replace.

citations: Jest is actively maintained under the OpenJS Foundation, ships regular releases, and continues improving ESM support and performance.
Vitest, meanwhile, has become the default in Vite, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, and most new Vue and React tooling because it shares a single transform pipeline with the dev server.
The version lacks a stable programmatic API, anticipated in 7.1.
test_runner_debugger_build.rationale: Jest and Vitest are both mature, actively maintained test runners with TypeScript-native support; VS Code and Node.js ship first-party debugging support; the build-tool ecosystem (webpack, Vite, esbuild, Rollup, swc, Rspack) is unusually broad and mature. Minor deduction because TypeScript 7.0 initially shipped without a stable programmatic compiler API, a temporary integration gap for tools that hook the compiler directly.

rubric.description: 0-100 score = sum of four 0-25 sub-scores: (1) package-manager availability/maturity/choice, (2) lockfile reproducibility and semver/versioning tooling, (3) workspace/monorepo support maturity, (4) security-auditing tooling maturity weighed against observed real-world supply-chain incident severity in the same window. Same sub-checks and evidence types apply to every language's package ecosystem.

ecosystem_scale_context.citation: As of May 15, 2026, the public npm registry replication endpoint reported about 4.04 million registry documents (doc_count: 4,038,347).
ecosystem_scale_context.note: Registry scale is recorded as contextual evidence only, not as a standalone proxy, per the frozen sampling rules.

citations: All four tools support this with the right flags: 'npm ci', 'yarn install --immutable', 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile', 'bun install --frozen-lockfile'.
For teams doing security audits or compliance reviews of their dependencies, human-readable lockfiles (npm, pnpm) are easier to audit.
lockfile_reproducibility.rationale: All major managers provide human-readable or binary lockfiles and a frozen/immutable install mode for CI reproducibility.

citations: npm ships with Node.js and dominates by default.

There is no universally best package manager in 2026. pnpm wins on disk efficiency and strict workspaces; Bun wins on raw install speed and runtime integration; Yarn 4 wins on PnP-style zero-installs; npm wins on compatibility
package_manager_maturity.rationale: npm ships by default with Node.js and is joined by mature, widely-adopted alternatives (pnpm, Yarn Berry, Bun) each with distinct strengths, giving TypeScript/JS projects unusually deep package-manager choice.

citations: Provenance attestations create a verifiable, cryptographically signed link (via Sigstore) between a published package version, the exact source commit that produced it, and the build system that ran the publish step.
npm v12 disables install scripts by default, and blocks git and remote-URL dependencies. The vector that carried Shai-Hulud is closed for anyone on v12.
On 11 May 2026 a worm published 84 malicious versions across 42 TanStack npm packages.
Every one of those versions carried a valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance attestation, signed through Sigstore, verifiable by any tool you point at it

From May to June 2026, various software supply chain attacks occurred via a self-spreading worm called Mini Shai-Hulud, attributed to hacker group TeamPCP, affecting companies such as GitHub, OpenAI, and Mercor.
security_auditing_vs_incidents.rationale: The ecosystem has real, actively-used auditing and provenance/attestation tooling (npm audit, Sigstore-backed provenance, trusted publishing, npm v12 disabling install scripts by default), but the same window saw severe, large-scale supply-chain incidents, including one where malicious versions carried fully valid provenance attestations, showing the current tooling detects but does not prevent sophisticated attacks.

citations: All four support monorepo workspaces, but with significant differences: npm's workspace support is functional for simple cases but lacks the advanced features pnpm and Yarn provide.
workspace_monorepo_support.rationale: All major managers support workspaces, but with real differences in depth; npm's implementation is functional yet the least advanced of the group.
